extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, engineers, geographers, anthropologists, and informed general readers interested in book reviews and topical commentary
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria used in this Nature issue's book and report reviews for judging scholarly and popular works (physics dictionaries, colonial reports, natural-history and geography books, history of astronomy). Emphasises accuracy, coverage, audience-fit, and practical consequences of authorial or editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and scope of reference work
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall plan (organization and selection of topics) should be coherent and appropriate to the work's stated purpose — e.g., follows earlier models but expands important sections while providing appropriate balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the plan gives adequate space to 'important sections' vs short articles; note if plan follows older models (Nichol) and whether that is appropriate. Example: the dictionary 'follows to a certain extent that adopted by Nichol, but the important sections are much larger.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A scholarly or technical book should cover the expected range of subjects for its field; omissions of significant modern topics are grounds for criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete missing topics (e.g., electric traction, electric ship-propulsion, electric vehicles, lightning-conductors) and judge whether their absence undermines the work's usefulness to intended readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and utility of an index
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference works should include a usable index; a name-index alone is insufficient for many readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an index is absent or limited to names (not subjects), readers — especially younger or non-specialist users — will have difficulty finding material. Example: 'The absence of an index makes it difficult ... There is a very elaborate name-index, but this will be little help.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of internationally agreed nomenclature and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internationally accepted names, units, symbols where possible rather than enforcing a rigid or idiosyncratic nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standard symbols/units; allow some variation when internationally agreed forms exist. Example praise: contributors 'had not been handicapped by being compelled to adopt a rigid nomenclature ... those agreed on internationally have been adopted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of formulas, equations, and technical statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical formulae and technical assertions must be correct and not misleading; misprints or algebraic omissions harm credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check equations for misprints and algebraic omissions (examples given: torque statement, missing term in algebraic reduction, wrong formulae for self-inductance). Note that concision should not cause inaccuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: State limitations and ranges for approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: When formulae or approximations are presented, their domain of validity and accuracy should be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting approximations without caveats. Example: formulae for capacity between circular plates are 'only approximations and no limitations to their accuracy are given.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical guidance for beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference texts should advise novices which methods or approaches are most suitable in common cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond listing methods, give recommendations or heuristics for method selection. Example: 'beginners would appreciate some little guidance as to which one to adopt in special cases.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate depth for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of mathematical/technical demand should match the target readership (e.g., little demand on mathematics for general users; deeper sections for specialists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether sections are 'substantial' enough for specialists without overburdening general readers. Example: 'little demand made on the reader's knowledge of mathematics' but also 'quite substantial books could be made of the sections.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and precision of terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading terms or inconsistent terminology (e.g., calling a variable quantity a 'constant'); use technically correct names for units and concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag terms that confuse specialists (example: dislike of the phrase 'dielectric constant' since it varies with temperature; use of 'absolute Centigrade scale' vs Kelvin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and correctness of units and nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Units and their names should conform to accepted standards or be clearly justified if irregular conventions are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note technically irregular usages (e.g., 'abcoulomb' etc.) and whether they are recognized by technical societies; avoid introducing new unit names without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality control and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be free of careless slips and misprints; such errors detract from value even if not fatal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document misprints and slips (equations, formula numbers, typographical errors); judge overall impact on usefulness. Example: 'We have noticed a few other slips and misprints. They do not appreciably detract, however, from the value of this volume.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of useful examples, tables, and rules-of-thumb
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tables, worked examples, and selection rules (e.g., choosing a galvanometer) increase a reference book's utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate usefulness of included tables and rules for practitioners (examples: tables for mutual inductance; rules for choosing a galvanometer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference completeness and citation usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include adequate bibliographic references so readers can pursue topics in depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large bibliographies (e.g., 'some 200 references') are valuable; ensure references are relevant and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive concision at expense of correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Conciseness is desirable, but not when it produces inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance brevity and precision; example criticism: 'occasionally his straining after conciseness leads him into inaccuracy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Match content to the stated or implied audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the book's content, depth, and organization suit the needs of the audience it addresses (e.g., young physicist vs factory test-room engineer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note mismatches where novices will struggle or specialists will find material superficial. Example: 'the younger physicist will have considerable difficulty in finding out what he wants.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original sources and awareness of historiography
rubrics_metrics.description: In historical scholarship, authors should consult original manuscripts and be familiar with the modern literature to avoid repeating outdated errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticise reliance on secondary authorities when primary sources or recent scholarship would correct mistakes. Example: the history of astronomy book 'never referring to the original sources' leads to errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and correct attribution in history
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical assertions (dates, attributions, technical achievements) must be accurate and properly attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify key facts (e.g., who asserted a given value for solar parallax, the content of Hipparchus's catalogue) against current scholarship; flag erroneous statements and misattributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up‑to‑date and current practical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel and practical guides must present current routing and infrastructural information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check railway/route statements and other logistics for currency; example: 'her information as to lines in the Eastern Alps is not entirely up-to-date.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage varied perspectives of intended activity (e.g., travel modes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works about activities (travel, fieldwork) should consider multiple ways of engaging (pedestrian, cyclist, automobilist) rather than a single mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value chapters that address the pedestrian/cyclist viewpoint in addition to railway or motor travel. Example: criticism that the author 'conducts us inevitably by railway' and 'overlooks the value of a continuous traverse by the pedestrian, the cyclist'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of accurate and appropriate place-names and local terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic and place-name usage should reflect contemporary and locally accepted forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer local or officially accepted names (example: prefer Bolzano to Botzen; Berne vs Bern) and avoid anglicized or outdated forms without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance, tolerance, and fair tone in cultural commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: When treating cultural subjects or peoples, the author should adopt an informed, tolerant, and balanced tone, not sweeping judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique hyperbolic or prejudiced statements and praise measured, sympathetic discussion. Example: 'her appreciation of the unconventional might have made her more tolerant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to social and cultural consequences of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports on administration or intervention in native societies should consider effects on authority, social fabric, and customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend sympathetic study of native custom, avoid actions that 'undermine authority and destroy a social fabric', and treat each case on its merits; cite examples like suppression of intertribal war having broad impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for native customs in administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonial or administrative policies should be conducted 'with due regard to native customs and institutions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether administration practices allow native development along lines in harmony with their culture and whether they provide opportunities for incorporation as responsible community elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hear and address tribal grievances patiently
rubrics_metrics.description: Good administration requires sympathetic treatment and patient hearing of tribal grievances to win confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate administrative reports for evidence of listening and remedial action; absence is a negative indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blanket prohibition; consider managed substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: When suppressing objectionable customs, consider substituting harmless elements rather than total suppression which may have unforeseen harmful effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: replace human victims with animals for ritual functions, or otherwise find harmless substitutes to retain social roles without harmful practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and literary quality (pleasantly written narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: For popular natural-history or travel books, readable style and good illustrations enhance value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise 'pleasantly written chapters' and rich illustrations; note when scientific results are deferred to specialized reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish popular narrative from scientific reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Field accounts may be valuable for illustration and impressions, but rigorous scientific results should be published separately in appropriate forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appraise whether the book makes clear what is personal observation vs what will be presented in formal scientific reports; example: 'The scientific results of the expedition ... will appear in due course.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to conservation and discussion of human impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural-history works should assess human impacts and threats to species, indicating conservation concerns where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's treatment of human colonization, overharvesting (eggs, hunting), and likely extinctions, and whether protective measures are discussed or suggested.
